newsitem.title: UK: Rolls Royce shrs rise after analyst meeting.
newsitem.headline: Rolls Royce shrs rise after analyst meeting.

text.p: Shares in Rolls Royce Plc extended their gains, climbing to a two-month high on Thursday, following an upbeat analysts meeting.
The shares, by far the best performer on the FTSE 100, added 15p, or 6.3 percent, to 254 by 1303 GMT. Turnover was 8.4 million shares, placing them on London's most active list.

Credit Lyonnais Laing analyst Daniel Bevan, who attended the meeting, said the company suggested that its profit margins in civil aerospace could return to those achieved in the 1980s at around 17 to 18 percent.
Bevan said he repeated his "buy" rating on the stock.
Dresdner Kleinwort Benson and SBC Warburg were also said to have had "buy" recommendations on the stock, but neither brokerage would comment.
Earlier, Rolls Royce raised its annual dividend and said it was negotiating the sale of its steam engine businesses, sparking the rally in the shares.

The company reported a pretax loss of 28 million stg after profits were wiped out by 263 million stg in provisions, write-offs and losses as a result of the group's decision to withdraw from steam power generation market.
But but the shares rose as analysts said the charges were already known and the underlying performance of the group was slightly ahead of expectations.
